title: GL-19 — EKS control plane then delete
beforeYouStart: Cost basis (us-east-1, priced 2026-09-29): EKS control plane, standard support, $0.10/cluster-hour (no node group in this lab); same-hour ≈ $0.20, forgotten 24 h ≈ $2.40. This is a floor: it excludes data transfer and LCU/usage charges. Re-read the pricing page before you run the lab.
stopChargesPanel: Delete the cluster and wait (EKS removes the cluster security group and network interfaces it created), then the IAM role; control plane bills hourly. Forgotten 24 h ≈ $2.40 (a floor; see the cost basis).

steps.title: Set the profile and region
bullets: In PowerShell run `$env:AWS_PROFILE = 'your-lab-profile'` using a named profile, not root.
Run `$env:AWS_REGION = 'us-east-1'`.
Success: both variables print the expected values.

steps.title: Confirm who is signed in
bullets: Run `aws sts get-caller-identity`.
Success: Arn contains `:user/` or `:assumed-role/`, not `:root`.
Set `$AccountId` from the Account field.

steps.title: Confirm AWS CLI v2
bullets: Run `aws --version`.
Success: output starts with `aws-cli/2`.
This lab focuses on EKS; Terraform is not required unless a step says so.

steps.title: Read the cost estimate
bullets: Open this lab's same-hour and forgotten-24h estimates in the card header.
Success: you can state both numbers before creating billable resources.
Budget alerts from GL-01 warn only; they do not stop spend.

steps.title: Accept cost risk
bullets: In the lab card, open the cost-risk box and type `I ACCEPT THE COST RISK` exactly as shown.
Success: the UI records your confirmation before any hourly resource is created.
Set `$CreatedAt` and `$ExpiresAt` to today's calendar date.

steps.title: EKS service role
bullets: Run `$Trust = @{Version='2012-10-17';Statement=@(@{Effect='Allow';Principal=@{Service='eks.amazonaws.com'};Action='sts:AssumeRole'})} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress; $utf8 = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false; [IO.File]::WriteAllText("$pwd\gl19-eks-trust.json", $Trust, $utf8)`. This writes the EKS cluster trust policy (Principal Service `eks.amazonaws.com`) as UTF-8 without a BOM.

Run `aws iam create-role --role-name workbook-gl19-eks --assume-role-policy-document file://gl19-eks-trust.json --tags Key=Workbook,Value=aws-tf-lab Key=LabId,Value=gl-19 Key=CreatedAt,Value=$CreatedAt Key=ExpiresAt,Value=$ExpiresAt`
Run `aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name workbook-gl19-eks --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonEKSClusterPolicy`.
Run `$EksRoleArn = aws iam get-role --role-name workbook-gl19-eks --query Role.Arn --output text`.
Success: role Arn is set.

steps.title: Create cluster
bullets: Run `$VpcId = aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=isDefault,Values=true --query "Vpcs[0].VpcId" --output text`.

Run `$Subnets = aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$VpcId Name=availability-zone-id,Values=use1-az1,use1-az2,use1-az4,use1-az6 --query "Subnets[0:2].SubnetId" --output text`. EKS rejects subnets in AZ ID use1-az3, and AZ names map to different AZ IDs per account, so subnets are filtered by availability-zone-id, not availability-zone.

Run `$SubnetIds = ($Subnets -split '\s+') | Where-Object { $_ }`. Run `aws eks create-cluster --name workbook-gl19 --role-arn $EksRoleArn --resources-vpc-config subnetIds=$($SubnetIds -join ',') --tags LabId=gl-19,Workbook=aws-tf-lab`.
Run `aws eks wait cluster-active --name workbook-gl19`.
Success: cluster status ACTIVE.

steps.title: Describe cluster
bullets: Run `aws eks describe-cluster --name workbook-gl19`.
Success: endpoint and version returned.

steps.title: Delete cluster
bullets: Run `aws eks delete-cluster --name workbook-gl19`.
Run `aws eks wait cluster-deleted --name workbook-gl19`.
Success: cluster deleted.

steps.title: Delete IAM role
bullets: Run `aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name workbook-gl19-eks --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonEKSClusterPolicy`.
Run `aws iam delete-role --role-name workbook-gl19-eks`.
Success: role is gone.

steps.title: Control plane cost note
bullets: EKS control plane bills per cluster-hour on standard support.
Success: cluster was deleted same session.

steps.title: Cost checkpoint
bullets: Confirm you typed `I ACCEPT THE COST RISK` in the card before any hourly create.

The EKS control plane bills per cluster-hour on standard support the entire time it exists, whether or not you run workloads; there are no managed nodes here to add compute cost, and the control plane cannot be stopped, only deleted.
Re-read the same-hour and forgotten-24h estimates on this lab card.
Success: you know what still bills if you walk away overnight.

steps.title: Order the deletes
bullets: Teardown order for this lab: EKS cluster, IAM role
Open Stop charges and read each PowerShell line top to bottom.
Success: dependents are deleted before parents.

steps.title: Tear the lab down
bullets: Run every Stop charges command yourself in order.
Success: `aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=gl-19` returns an empty ResourceTagMappingList.

steps.title: Check the bill later
bullets: After 8–12 hours, review today's charges in the Billing console.
Record actual spend in your notes.
Leftover tagged resources (the EKS cluster) can still bill per cluster-hour until deleted.

hints: Use official AWS docs for exact flags.

verification: aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=gl-19 returns an empty ResourceTagMappingList in $env:AWS_REGION
teardown.stillBillingNote: Time already used, transfer, tax, and 8–12h billing lag may still appear. Alerts do not delete resources.
teardown.recovery: If teardown fails, stop. Confirm $env:AWS_REGION is us-east-1 and the caller is not root. Run aws sts get-caller-identity and type that Account value before any delete. List LabId=gl-19 with aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=LabId,Values=gl-19. Delete only those ids. Never delete untagged resources.

body: EKS cluster on standard support with no managed nodes, then delete cluster same day.
